question: Will the UK increase the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years before May 2026?
summary: Objections correctly flag legislative and timing risk that could delay any change beyond May 2026.
Official materials explicitly propose a 10-year baseline ('Earned Settlement'), with public consultation through Feb 2026 and possible implementation from April 2026.
Despite the risk, the policy direction is clear and momentum exists, justifying a net probability above the current ensemble's 35%.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and reveal a genuine, non-implausible risk that legislative timing could derail the May 2026 target.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted probability upward to 0.58 from 0.35 to reflect substantive momentum and explicit policy proposals, with a range reflecting remaining legislative uncertainty. No downward bias due to implausible-threshold concerns.

forecasts.reference-class: UK immigration policy reforms proposing to raise the standard settlement qualifying period from 5 years to 10 years (Earned Settlement) and the accompanying public consultation process.

sources.claim: The Earned Settlement consultation states the default qualifying period for settlement will be increased to 10 years, with a time-adjustment model and four pillars guiding earned settlement.
Migration Observatory summarizes that the standard waiting period to settlement would rise from 5 to 10 years, with exceptions, and that the public consultation runs into February 2026.
GOV.UK confirms the long residence route requires a 10-year qualifying period for settlement, illustrating the presence of a 10-year threshold in current rules.
Long residence guidance details the 10-year qualifying period and how it is calculated for settlement under Appendix Long Residence.
The default qualifying period for settlement will be increased from five to ten years; the government is consulting on how this might be implemented.
The 2025 immigration white paper proposed increasing the standard qualifying period for permanent residence to ten years, with final decisions following public consultation (completed Feb 2026).
Editorial/opinion arguing that moving to a 10-year ILR is controversial and potentially unfair.
Migration Observatory analysis outlining expected longer waiting periods for many categories and the 10-year baseline under consideration.
Long residence route already uses a 10-year qualifying period, illustrating that a 10-year baseline is a plausible anchor for settlement policy but via a different route.
Petitions opposing the 10-year ILR proposal; the government indicated that no decision had been taken on applying changes to people already in the UK.
Earned settlement proposal to increase standard qualifying period for settlement to ten years, with a time-adjustment model based on four pillars.
House of Commons Library briefing summarises the government proposal to move to a ten-year baseline and exceptional routes; consultation details.
The 24 June 2025 changes provide background on how qualifying periods are calculated and the broader context for longer residence requirements.
Migration Observatory analysis outlining expected longer waiting periods for many migrants under proposed settlement changes and the consultation timeline.
Guardian reporting on government proposals to extend waiting period for permanent settlement from five to ten years.
Guardian reporting IPPR estimate of impact on children under proposed settlement timeline changes.
